newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ex-ruler gets back passport.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ex-ruler gets back passport.

text.p: Bangladesh authorities have returned former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad's passport, which was seized after he was overthrown six years ago, police said on Monday.
They said Ershad received his passport on Sunday in hospital where he is recovering from severe chest pain.

Leaders of Ershad's Jatiya Party said he might go abroad soon for medical treatment. "His trip outside for treatment has been long overdue but delayed because he did not have his passport," one leader said on Monday.
Ershad, 68, has been admitted to hospital twice this year.
Last week police returned Ershad's firearms which were seized from his residence in January 1991, weeks after he was deposed in an uprising.

"We gave the firearms back to Ershad on Thursday in his hospital," a police officer said. "This was done in pursuance of a court verdict (two years ago) that Ershad possessed the firearms legally and they should be restored to him," he said.
Ershad, a former army strongman, took power in a 1982 bloodless coup. He was deposed in a people's uprising in December 1990 and sent to jail.
He was sentenced to 10-years in prison for keeping the arms illegally but the country's High Court overturned the conviction in June 1995 and ordered him to be freed.
But Ershad remained in prison until January 1997 when he was granted bail on 19 other charges of corruption and misuse of power.
Ershad was elected a Jatiya Party legislator in the June 1996 election which he contested from jail.
